findings.title: Second FLY-2567 suite still asserts the reconciled ACK receipt is consumed; CI-gated and now red
findings.detail: b799c34f4 removed `this.ack(pendingAck.id, input.now)` from the expiry-settlement branch of reconcileExpiredLeases (packages/flywheel-comm/src/mailbox-queue.ts:2133) so the ack_batch protocol receipt stays claimable for ProtocolIngress. The author updated the FLY-2567 expectations in src/__tests__/mailbox-queue.test.ts (lines 138/150, ACKED→QUEUED) but missed the second FLY-2567 suite: src/__tests__/mailbox-queue-capabilities.test.ts:140 still asserts `expect(queue.getById("queued-ack")?.state).toBe("ACKED")`. Measured at d130140: `vitest run src/__tests__/mailbox-queue-capabilities.test.ts` gives `52 tests | 2 failed` — scenario `queued` (expected 'QUEUED' to be 'ACKED') and scenario `expired-claim` (expected 'LEASED' to be 'ACKED'); the other 50 pass and result.requeued/member-state assertions are unaffected, so only the receipt-state line is stale. This is a merge gate: .github/workflows/ci.yml:204 runs `pnpm --filter flywheel-comm ... test:run`, and flywheel-comm's test:run is a bare `vitest run` over the whole package. The branch lands CI-red. This is the same class of miss as round 1's shell gate — grep the repo for every assertion on the receipt row, not just the suite you were editing. Fix: update line 140 to the new contract (QUEUED for `queued`, LEASED-with-stale-claim for `expired-claim`) and state in the test name/comment that ingress, not the reconciler, finalizes the receipt.

findings.title: Summary identity projection is incomplete: FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_ASSIGNMENT_DIGEST still stripped
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head and reported as governance-settled in validation.md, so re-listed as a non-blocking advisory with the same id. FULL_ACCESS_ENV_ALLOWLIST carries ROLE/DUTY/GRANULARITY but not FLYWHEEL_SUMMARY_ASSIGNMENT_DIGEST, which canonical_lead_identity_resolve exports alongside them (packages/teamlead/scripts/lib/canonical-lead-identity.sh:171-174) and which packages/flywheel-comm/src/commands/summary.ts:120-126 requires. Raya (recipient, duty=false) only needs the merge-authority tuple, so the reported summary_merge_authority_required incident is covered. growth/mufasa-lead is also a full-access Codex Lead and resolves to producer/duty=true with a digest, so a summary submission from that pane now fails at summary_assignment_digest_invalid instead of summary_duty_required — still blocked. The milestone now says the PR does not claim producer capability, which is an acceptable scope statement; no code change needed for this PR.

findings.title: Non-authoritative StateStore mirror can still fail the already-committed batch ACK
findings.detail: protocol-ingress.ts is byte-identical to round 1, so this stands. The mirror loop runs unguarded after queue.ackBatchByRecipient has committed the mailbox ACK; if getLeadEventBySeq or markSummaryAbsorptionAcked throws (teamlead.db SQLITE_BUSY during a lead-restart herd), handle() throws and LeadInboxLoop (lead-inbox-loop.ts:266-289) records a bridge delivery failure, retries, then dead-letters the row and fires onProtocolQuarantine — for a batch that is genuinely settled in CommDB. The R2 reconciler change actually widens the window slightly: the receipt now survives expiry settlement and is retried by ingress, so a persistently failing StateStore write burns the retry budget on a row that previously would have been consumed by the reconciler. Since the code documents this write as a mirror of the canonical mailbox receipt, wrap the loop in try/catch + console.warn (the duplicate-receipt replay already repairs it on the next receipt) so a non-authoritative write cannot quarantine an authoritative ACK.

findings.title: Expiry-settled receipts for a Lead with no inbox loop are now never disposed
findings.detail: New in R2. Previously reconcileExpiredLeases finalized the receipt itself, so the row reached a terminal state regardless of who was draining. Now the only consumer is LeadInboxLoop via claimBridgeProtocol({fromAgent: leadId}) — confirmed the sole caller in packages/ (mailbox-queue.ts:2647 is called only from lead-inbox-loop.ts:254). If a Lead is retired or removed from projects.json while one of its batches expires with a durably queued ack_batch, the reconciler settles the members and the recipient_kind='bridge' receipt stays QUEUED forever: the lead terminal sweep only touches `batch_id = ?` members, the maxTerminalRows terminal scan is runner-only, and the retention/archive engine only moves ACKED/DEAD rows. No counter, backpressure or alert reads queued bridge rows (the only other references are the two claim indexes in mailbox-schema.ts:266/269), so impact is a small durable residue rather than a stall. Worth a bounded disposal path or an explicit note that bridge protocol rows have no sweeper.

findings.title: Canonical delivery id re-derived inline instead of via canonicalLeadEventDeliveryId
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The binding check hardcodes `lead_event:${event.lead_id}:${event.event_id}` while the producer (lead-event-queue.ts:8-13) builds it as `envelope.eventId?.trim() || \`seq:${envelope.seq}\``. For a journal row whose event_id is empty or whitespace-padded the real delivery_id is `lead_event:<lead>:seq:<n>`, so the comparison never matches and the mirror silently skips a legitimate receipt. summary_absorption_round always carries a non-empty roundId, so this is latent, but the two derivations can drift. Call canonicalLeadEventDeliveryId(leadEventEnvelopeFromJournalRow(event)) — both symbols are already imported by the test file — so there is one definition.

findings.title: Summary identity forwarded into the lead_actions MCP child that never reads it
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The three summary names are appended to envVarNames unconditionally, so they are forwarded into the lead_actions MCP child and pinned into the exact-match §10 gate. Nothing under packages/teamlead/src/lead-backends/codex/lead-actions/ reads them (parseLeadActionsConfig ignores them) and runner-actions.ts spawns nothing from env; the fix that matters for the incident is the FULL_ACCESS_ENV_ALLOWLIST entry feeding the pane shell where flywheel-comm runs. The cost is concrete — it is what forced the two shell-gate edits in R2. Either drop the envVarNames half or record the intended future consumer in the comment.
